# 2.2 · Neurons and Layers

`Level 2: Tiny Autograd` · `+25 XP` · `drill 2 of 3`

## The job
Stack `Value`s into a network. A `Neuron` computes tanh(w . x + b) (or just w . x + b when
`nonlin=False`). A `Layer` is a list of neurons that all see the same inputs. An `MLP`
chains layers: tanh in the hidden layers, a linear last layer, a single `Value` out when
the last layer has one neuron. Every piece reports its `parameters()`.

## Why it matters
"Count the parameters" is the first sanity check on any architecture, and "the output
layer must be linear for regression" is a real bug people ship. Building the containers
yourself also explains what `model.parameters()` and `optimizer.zero_grad()` are for.

## Run it

```bash
python fullsend.py check 2.2     # judge your drill.py
python fullsend.py hint 2.2      # one hint at a time
```

<details><summary>All hints (try the drill first)</summary>

1. Start the weighted sum at the bias: `sum((w * x for ...), self.b)` keeps everything as Values.
2. Raise ValueError when a neuron gets the wrong number of inputs. Silent zip truncation hides shape bugs.
3. For layer sizes, pair up consecutive dimensions: [n_in] + sizes gives (n_in, s0), (s0, s1), ...
4. Only the last layer is linear: nonlin is True for every layer index except the final one.

</details>
